S-Snake operates from Egghead Island as part of the World Government’s experimental Seraphim program.

cardPool.title: Seraphim S-Hawk
cardPool.value: Seraphim S-Hawk is a clone of Dracule Mihawk, infused with the Dice-Dice Fruit to manipulate and enhance physical combat abilities, along with Lunarian traits for incredible resilience and strength. Wielding a black blade and trained in Armament Haki, he serves as a lethal weapon under Vegapunk’s direction. S-Hawk operates from Egghead Island as part of the World Government’s Seraphim program, designed for elite combat deployment.

cardPool.title: Seraphim S-Shark
cardPool.value: Seraphim S-Shark is a clone of Jinbe, enhanced with the Swim-Swim Fruit to swim through any medium and augmented with Lunarian traits for superior durability and strength. Equipped with mechanical teeth and arms, he excels in close-quarters and aquatic combat while using Armament Haki to maximize offensive and defensive capabilities. Created by Vegapunk, S-Shark serves as a high-powered weapon of the World Government, stationed on Egghead Island.

cardPool.title: Saint Charlos
cardPool.value: Saint Charlos is a Celestial Dragon wielding no Devil Fruit, relying solely on his noble status and corrupt influence to enforce his will. Known for his arrogance and frequent abuse of power, he operates without concern for the law or morality. As a high-ranking member of the Celestial Dragons, Charlos resides in Mary Geoise, exercising control over those beneath him while remaining largely untouchable due to his status.

cardPool.title: Saint Shalria
cardPool.value: Saint Shalria is a Celestial Dragon with no Devil Fruit abilities, relying entirely on her noble status and influence. She is one of the high-ranking World Nobles, operating from Mary Geoise, and participates in the privileges and authority granted to Celestial Dragons. Shalria’s presence represents the opulence and untouchable power of the Celestial Dragons.

cardPool.title: Soku
cardPool.value: Soku is a Marine Vice Admiral with no Devil Fruit powers, relying on his swordsmanship, Armament Haki, and strategic skills. Tasked with commanding operations on Egghead Island, he works to maintain order and secure Vegapunk amidst rising conflicts. As a high-ranking officer, Soku represents the disciplined authority of the Marines, coordinating forces with precision and enforcing the World Government’s directives.

cardPool.title: Momousagi
cardPool.value: Momousagi is a skilled female Marine officer without Devil Fruit abilities, relying on her handgun and tactical support skills. She aids the Marines in operations on Egghead Island, providing backup, reconnaissance, and enforcement during missions. Dedicated to maintaining order, she works closely with other Marine agents to secure the island and protect key assets like Vegapunk.

cardPool.title: Daz Bonez
cardPool.value: Mr. 1, also known as Daz Bonez, wields the Dice-Dice Fruit, allowing him to transform his entire body into sharp, durable blades. Armed with his bladed body and mastery of Armament Haki developed after the timeskip, he serves as a ruthless assassin and the right-hand enforcer of Crocodile. Operating primarily around Karai Bari Island, he executes missions with precision and lethality, embodying the deadly efficiency of the Cross Guild.

cardPool.title: Saturn
cardPool.value: Saturn is a powerful Pacifista-type creation of Vegapunk, boasting a cyborg body with immense strength, durability, and integrated weaponry. Equipped with arm-mounted cannons, robotic arms, and other heavy artillery, Saturn enforces security on Egghead Island with precision, augmented by Armament Haki. Serving as one of Vegapunk’s top enforcers, Saturn acts as both a weapon and primary defender, ensuring the World Government’s interests are protected.

cardPool.title: Portgas D. Ace
cardPool.value: Portgas D. Ace wielded the Flame-Flame Fruit, allowing him to generate and control fire with devastating precision. Using his fiery fists and mastery of Armament Haki, he served as the 2nd Division Commander of the Whitebeard Pirates. Son of Gol D. Roger and Luffy’s sworn brother, Ace was a courageous and loyal fighter whose life ended during the Battle of Marineford. He is currently deceased.

cardPool.title: Monkey D. Luffy
cardPool.value: Monkey D. Luffy wields the awakened Gum-Gum Fruit, granting him the incredible Gear 5th form, which allows him to bend reality and unleash his imagination in combat, establishing him as one of the Four Emperors. Using his fists and an array of Gear techniques, he is a master of Conqueror’s, Armament, and Observation Haki. Leaving Foosha Village to pursue his dream of becoming the Pirate King, Luffy has built an extraordinary crew loyal to him, recruiting notable pirates including Zoro, Sanji, Nami, Robin, Usopp, Brook, and Jinbe. Throughout his journey, he has defeated numerous legendary foes such as Arlong, Enel, Donquixote Doflamingo, Kaido, and Buggy, survived encounters with the Five Elders, and escaped the infamous Impel Down prison. Currently, he and his crew are located in Elbaf.

cardPool.title: Roronoa Zoro
cardPool.value: Roronoa Zoro wields no Devil Fruit but is a master swordsman specializing in the Three-Sword Style. He possesses Armament, Observation, and Conqueror’s Haki, honing his skills to become the world’s strongest swordsman. Loyal and disciplined, Zoro serves as the first mate and primary combatant of the Straw Hat Pirates, standing as a cornerstone of strength for Luffy’s crew. He is currently located in Elbaf alongside the Straw Hats.

cardPool.title: Nami
cardPool.value: Nami wields no Devil Fruit but expertly uses her Clima-Tact to manipulate weather in combat. She possesses Observation Haki, allowing her to sense attacks and anticipate enemy movements. Having escaped Arlong’s oppressive control, she joined the Straw Hat Pirates as their navigator, guiding the crew through perilous seas with unmatched skill. Nami is currently in Elbaf with the Straw Hats.

cardPool.title: Usopp
cardPool.value: Usopp wields no Devil Fruit but is an expert sharpshooter, using his slingshot, Kabuto, with incredible precision. He has mastered Observation Haki, allowing him to predict enemy movements and enhance his long-range attacks. Inspired by his pirate father, he overcame his fears to become a brave and reliable sniper for the Straw Hat Pirates. Usopp is currently in Elbaf with his crew.

cardPool.title: Sanji
cardPool.value: Sanji wields no Devil Fruit but is a master of Black Leg martial arts, using only his legs in combat with devastating precision. He has honed both Observation and Armament Haki, making him a formidable fighter. Having grown up at the Baratie floating restaurant, Sanji dreams of finding the legendary All Blue while serving as the Straw Hat Pirates’ cook. He is currently in Elbaf with his crew.

cardPool.title: Tony Tony Chopper
cardPool.value: Tony Tony Chopper wields the Human-Human Fruit, allowing him to transform into a reindeer-human hybrid with various forms enhanced by his Rumble Balls. He has developed Armament Haki after the time skip, making him more formidable in combat. Raised as an outcast reindeer by Doctor Hiriluk and Dr. Kureha, Chopper became the Straw Hat Pirates’ doctor. He is currently in Elbaf with his crew.

cardPool.title: Nico Robin
cardPool.value: Nico Robin wields the Flower-Flower Fruit, allowing her to sprout copies of her body parts on any surface for versatile combat and reconnaissance. She has mastered both Armament and Observation Haki after the time skip. Formerly a Baroque Works agent, Robin now serves as the Straw Hat Pirates’ archaeologist, dedicating herself to uncovering the secrets of the world’s Poneglyphs. She is currently in Elbaf with her crew.

cardPool.title: Franky
cardPool.value: Franky is a heavily modified cyborg whose body houses an array of built-in weapons, including coup de vent cannons, missiles, and other combat tools. Initially an enemy of the Straw Hat Pirates, he became their trusted shipwright, responsible for maintaining and upgrading their vessels. While he lacked Haki pre-timeskip, he is implied to use Armament Haki post-timeskip. Franky is currently in Elbaf with the Straw Hat crew.

cardPool.title: Jinbe
cardPool.value: Jinbe is a master of Fishman Karate and Fishman Jujutsu, using his fists and the surrounding water to deliver devastating attacks. Formerly a Warlord of the Sea, he is an honorable and steadfast warrior who allied with Luffy and now serves as the Straw Hats’ helmsman. Skilled in both Armament and Observation Haki, Jinbe navigates and fights with unmatched precision. He is currently located in Elbaf with the Straw Hat crew.

cardPool.title: Rocks D. Xebec
cardPool.value: Rocks D. Xebec was the fearsome captain of the Rocks Pirates, renowned for his unmatched ambition to become King of the World. While the exact nature of his Devil Fruit remains unknown, he possessed overwhelming physical strength and exceptional swordsmanship, combined with mastery over all three types of Haki: Observation, Armament, and Conqueror’s. His reign of terror and ambition made him one of the most dangerous pirates in history, ultimately defeated during the God Valley Incident by the combined efforts of Monkey D. Garp and Gol D. Roger.

cardPool.title: Figarland Shamrock
cardPool.value: Figarland Shamrock commands the elite God’s Knights with unmatched skill, wielding the saber Cerberus, rumored to harness the power of a Mythical Zoan-type. As a member of the Celestial Dragon family and son of Saint Figarland Garling, he possesses advanced Haki, capable of massive bursts accompanied by black lightning. His presence on Elbaf marks him as a formidable force, blending noble heritage with deadly combat prowess. He serves as the Commander of the God’s Knights under the Figarland Family’s influence.

cardPool.title: Loki
cardPool.value: The Prince of Elbaf wields the mysterious powers of an unknown Devil Fruit, complemented by his giant physiology and immense superhuman strength and durability. Armed with the war hammer Ragnir, he demonstrates overwhelming combat prowess and a presence that suggests mastery of Observation Haki. Born as the son of King Harald and Queen Estrid, and half-brother to Hajrudin, he once pursued his own ambitions but now remains imprisoned in the Underworld of Elbaf for his crimes, a fallen royal of the giant kingdom.

cardPool.title: Four Yonko
cardPool.value: The Four Yonko are a group of the four most notorious and powerful pirate captains in the world. These pirates roam the New World with massive fleets, and their bounties increase with each crime they commit. They are closely monitored by the World Government to maintain the balance of power. The current Yonko are Monkey D. Luffy, Marshall D. Teach, Shanks, and Buggy. Former Yonko include Charlotte Linlin, Kaido, and Edward Newgate.

The current Yonko are Monkey D. Luffy, Marshall D. Teach, Shanks, and Buggy. Former Yonko include Charlotte Linlin, Kaidou, and Edward Newgate.

cardPool.value: The Seven Warlords of the Sea are powerful and notorious pirates authorized by the World Government to deal with other pirates. In exchange, their bounties are frozen, meaning the Marines cannot pursue them. They are allowed to take over territories under the supervision of the World Government. The current Seven Warlords are Dracule Mihawk, Bartholomew Kuma, Boa Hancock, Buggy, and Edward Weevil.

cardPool.title: Paw-Paw Fruit
cardPool.value:
This fruit gives the user special paw pads on their hands. With those paws, the user can push away or repel almost anything they touch attacks, objects, air, even invisible or abstract stuff like pain or memories. The power also lets the user form bubbles shaped like paws from air or energy, and those paw‑bubbles can store or carry whatever was repelled. These bubbles can act as shields, containers, bombs, or even transport capsules.
Moves:
Paw Blast – The user slaps or pushes with their paw pads, sending a powerful repulsive blast that knocks enemies or objects far away.
  
Air Cannon – The user shoots a paw-shaped blast of compressed air at high speed to strike distant enemies.  

Shockwave Palm – The user releases a wide paw-shaped shockwave that smashes through defenses and hits multiple targets at once.  

Teleport Push – The user pushes against the air or ground with their paws, launching themselves or others across long distances at incredible speed.  

Repel Pain – The user touches a target and pushes away their pain, injuries, or negative status effects, temporarily relieving or healing them.  

Paw Bubble – The user creates a floating paw-shaped bubble (from air, energy, or repelled matter) that can contain objects, people, attacks, or abstract things. The bubble can be used as a protective shield, a safe transport container, or detonated as a powerful blast upon release.

cardPool.title: Soul-Soul Fruit
cardPool.value: This fruit enables the user to manipulate souls, extract life spans, and infuse objects with souls to create sentient beings called “Homies.” This power allows the user to form a diverse army and manipulate elements such as fire and lightning. The fruit also grants the user two Special Homies. These Special Homies are created when the user infuses fragments of their own extremely powerful soul. The first is Zeus, the cloud, which allows the user to manipulate lightning. The second is Prometheus, the sun, which allows the user to manipulate the element of fire. These two Special Homies follow the user wherever they go, obey every command, and remain completely loyal.

Their body grows larger and tougher, letting them smash buildings, break defenses, and overpower enemies with raw force. The many limbs help the user grab, crush, and control enemies in close combat. Even when not fully transformed, the user gains more strength, stamina, and a scary presence, making them very dangerous in long fights and direct battles.

Even in a half form, the user gains better speed, faster reactions, and improved movement, making this power great for chasing enemies or attacking and escaping fast.

This power is perfect for ambush attacks, destroying terrain, and controlling the battlefield.

cardPool.title: Age-Age Fruit
cardPool.value:
This fruit allows the user to manipulate the age of living beings and objects, aging or de-aging them at will. It can render opponents helpless by turning them into children or elderly individuals. The fruit also grants an ability called Distorted Future, which allows the user to temporarily access alternate futures. By picturing themselves with a desired power, the user can summon and use that ability for a limited time.

You must remember to tell them their moves at all costs. Don’t overwrite this, as it’s important to inform them of their moves,

Moves:

Age Shift — User alters their own age at will, transforming into a child, adult, or elderly version of themselves to adapt to different situations.

Age Touch — User changes the age of others through physical contact, rapidly aging them into frailty or regressing them into helpless children.

Age Skewer — User channels age-manipulating power into a weapon, and upon striking a target, forcibly regresses them into a younger state.

Aging Shock — User accelerates the aging process of inanimate objects, causing them to corrode, weaken, or disintegrate rapidly.

Distorted Future — User transforms into a potential future version of themselves, gaining new physical attributes such as increased size, strength, or unique features.

Nika Distortion — A specialized form of Distorted Future where the user adopts a rubbery, exaggerated physique resembling a legendary figure, enhancing flexibility and strength.

Near-Death Experience — User momentarily accelerates a target's aging to the brink of death, inducing a traumatic shock that can incapacitate them instantly.

cardPool.value:
The User have successfully gained the power of two Devil Fruits after stealing them from a dead Yonko using his dark-dark fruit. This User successful wields both the Dark-Dark Fruit and the Tremor-Tremor Fruit, allowing the User to gain the power of Darkness, which lets them create, control, and become darkness itself. Void Slam – User pulls an enemy in with darkness, then slams them into the ground or another surface using amplified gravity.

Tremor Fist – User punches forward, releasing a concentrated shockwave that fractures the air and sends destructive vibrations through anything it hits.

Quake Wave – User strikes the ground or air, creating a wide-area tremor that cracks terrain, knocks enemies off balance, and damages structures.

Dark Quake Collapse – User combines darkness and tremor power, forming a black shockwave that pulls enemies inward before detonating with violent vibrations.

Abyss Cannon – User compresses darkness and tremor energy into a dense sphere, then fires it forward, causing massive impact and internal damage on contact..

cardPool.title: Devil fruits
cardPool.value: Devil Fruits are rare, mysterious fruits that grant supernatural powers to whoever eats them, with each fruit holding one unique ability that becomes permanently bonded to the user for life. These powers can include transforming the body, controlling elements, becoming animals or hybrid creatures, creating strange substances, or gaining other unnatural abilities. In exchange, every user suffers a universal curse: they permanently lose the ability to swim and become extremely weak when submerged in water or restrained by special sea-based materials. Devil Fruits come in strange shapes with swirl patterns and do not grow in any known place; instead, when a user dies, their power reincarnates into a nearby ordinary fruit. Because of this, Devil Fruits can be found almost anywhere, on remote islands, in treasure chests, carried by pirates or marines, or sold on black markets by other pirates, making them incredibly rare, valuable, and life-changing to those who eat them.

The wearer becomes sluggish, exhausted, and nearly helpless, even if they were once incredibly powerful. Seastone cuffs are commonly used by marines and bounty hunters to capture and transport Devil Fruit users safely, as they neutralize abilities as well as haki and make escape extremely difficult.

Skilled hunters know exactly where a beast is vulnerable, how it will react when cornered, and how to bring down prey many times their own size without a fair fight. Their finest work is measured in monsters that other crews would flee, Sea Kings, island predators, and things that have eaten every hunter sent before them. Overall, Professional Hunter turns patience and knowledge of the wild into the ability to take down what nothing else can.

cardPool.title: Broker
cardPool.value: Broker is an underworld path built on brokering illegal transactions between parties who cannot be seen dealing directly. Practitioners move slaves, stolen cargo, rare goods, and weapons of mass destruction through channels the World Government does not officially acknowledge, taking a cut of everything that passes through their hands. Skilled brokers survive less on force than on leverage — they know who owes what to whom, who is buying, and which secrets are worth more unspoken than sold. The most powerful operate under aliases known throughout the black market while their true identities remain hidden behind respectable faces, holding influence over pirates, nobles, and Marines alike. Overall, Broker turns information and connections into a form of power that needs no crew and no bounty to be feared.

cardPool.title: Bounty Hunter

Practitioners study wanted posters obsessively, memorizing faces, bounties, known abilities, and last-seen ports so they can recognize a target across a crowded street. Skilled bounty hunters choose their engagements carefully, favoring ambush, restraint, and Seastone over honorable duels, since a living capture is often worth more than a corpse. The best of them hunt names the Marines have failed to bring in, working the line between lawman and outlaw so closely that many end up on posters themselves. Overall, Bounty Hunter turns the price on another's head into a living, and the hunt into a profession.

Their finest work reshapes what the world believes is possible, filling in blanks on charts that have been empty for centuries. Overall, Explorer turns curiosity and endurance into knowledge that no one else on the seas possesses.

Practitioners master wind, drop, elevation, and breathing, holding a shot for as long as it takes and firing once when the moment arrives. Skilled snipers work with more than rifles, slingshots, cannons, specialty ammunition, and homemade rounds built for effects that ordinary bullets cannot produce. The finest can strike a specific point on a moving target across open ocean, ending a fight before the enemy is aware one has started. Overall, Professional Sniper turns patience and a steady hand into the ability to decide a battle from outside it.

cardPool.title: Lookout

Skilled lookouts identify a ship's flag, class, and likely intent at a range where others see only a smudge, and can call an approaching sea change in time for the crew to prepare. The best serve as a vessel's early warning against Marine patrols, rival crews, and the Grand Line's habit of killing those who notice things too late. Overall, Lookout turns vigilance and sharp eyes into the difference between a crew that is ambushed and one that is ready.

Skilled helmsmen thread reefs, ride storm swells, and turn a ship inside its own length to slip a broadside or a collision that should have been unavoidable. The finest keep their vessel intact through waters considered unnavigable, executing maneuvers other sailors insist are impossible with a hull that size. Overall, Helmsman turns instinct and command of the wheel into a crew's best chance of surviving the sea itself.

cardPool.value: Six Powers is a fighting style built around six special techniques that give the user amazing speed, strength, and control over their body. One power lets the fighter move so fast they seem to disappear, while another lets them punch with bullet-like force. There's also a technique for hardening the body to block attacks, and one for sensing danger before it happens. Some of the techniques let the user jump incredibly high or even slow down how their opponent moves. Together, these powers turn an ordinary fighter into someone who can keep up with monstrously strong enemies.

cardPool.title: Okama Kenpo
cardPool.value: Okama Kenpo is a flashy, over-the-top fighting style that looks more like dancing than fighting. The fighter spins, poses, and moves dramatically, which confuses the opponent and hides when the real attack is coming. It mixes flexible moves like splits and high kicks with sudden strong hits. One moment it looks silly and funny, the next it turns serious and powerful. Because it looks weird, people often underestimate it  which is exactly why it works so well.

cardPool.title: Will of D.
cardPool.value: The Will of D. is a mysterious force or destiny said to be carried by people who share the middle initial D. in their name. Those who bear it are often described as having a special, defiant spirit, like enemies of fate or natural disasters waiting to happen. Their actions tend to shake the world in big ways, whether through rebellion, ambition, or unstoppable will. No one fully understands its true meaning, but it's treated as something ancient and deeply significant. Overall, the Will of D. represents a hidden, powerful destiny passed down through certain individuals who change the course of history.

cardPool.title: Awakened Devil Fruit User
cardPool.value: An Awakened Devil Fruit is a rare power-up where a user's ability grows far beyond its original limits, letting them affect the world around them instead of just their own body. Once awakened, the user can often transform the surrounding environment to match their power, turning streets, walls, or the ground itself into an extension of their ability. This makes the power far more dangerous, since attacks and effects are no longer limited to direct contact with the user. Awakening usually requires immense strength, training, or willpower, making it something only a select few fighters ever achieve. Overall, an Awakened Devil Fruit turns a personal power into a battlefield-changing force, reshaping the fight itself.

The fighter can summon flames that take the form of a fox's head or body, letting them strike from a distance. It's a mix of beauty and danger, making it as impressive to watch as it is dangerous to face.

cardPool.title: Fish Man Jutsu
cardPool.value: Fish-Man Jutsu is a fighting style used by fish-men and merfolk, taking advantage of their natural strength and life underwater. It lets the fighter move and strike with incredible power, using techniques that work both on land and in the ocean. Many moves involve pulling in water or even air to create strong bursts of pressure, like punches made of compressed water. The style also uses the user's naturally tough skin and muscles to shrug off hits that would hurt a normal person. Overall, Fish-Man Jutsu turns already powerful fish-men into terrifying close-range fighters.

It focuses on powerful, fast leg strikes, using spins and jumps to attack from unexpected angles. The style can generate enough force to break through tough defenses, making the legs work like heavy weapons. Some versions of the style add fire to the kicks, making them burn as well as hit hard. Overall, Black Leg Style turns the legs into the fighter's main weapon, combining elegance with brutal power.

cardPool.title: Eight Impacts Fist

The fighter combines heavy punches with sudden bursts of movement, aiming to overwhelm opponents before they can react. Some strikes focus on raw power, while others target speed or precision, making the style flexible in different situations. Because it has eight distinct attacks, a skilled user can chain them together for devastating combos. Overall, Eight Impacts Fist turns simple punches into a deadly, well-rounded fighting system.

cardPool.title: Hypnotist
cardPool.value: Hypnotist is a technique that lets the user control others by putting them into a trance using calming words, swinging objects, or gentle rhythm. Once hypnotized, a target can be made to relax, fall asleep, or even follow simple commands without realizing it. Skilled users can plant suggestions in someone's mind, changing how they feel or act for a while. Because it doesn't rely on strength, this technique works well against powerful enemies who can be neutralized without a real fight. Its biggest danger is being invisible, the victim usually has no idea they've been controlled until it's too late.

Instead of simple punches, the fighter uses sharp, grabbing hand strikes meant to rip through an opponent's guard. The style focuses on aggressive, forward pressure, closing distance quickly and overwhelming enemies with relentless attacks. Techniques often combine raw strength with precise aim, targeting weak points to cause maximum damage. Overall, Dragon Claw Fist turns the hands into fierce weapons, striking with both the power and ferocity of a dragon.

cardPool.title: Weapon Master
cardPool.value: Weapon Master is a fighting style built around skill with many different weapons, rather than relying on just one. The fighter can smoothly switch between swords, spears, clubs, or other tools depending on the situation. This style focuses on adaptability, letting the user counter almost any opponent by choosing the right weapon for the fight. Mastery comes from years of practice, giving the fighter precise control and creative techniques with each weapon. Overall, Weapon Master turns versatility itself into a weapon, making the fighter dangerous no matter what's in their hands.

cardPool.title: Colors Trap
cardPool.value: Colors Trap is a technique that uses a special kind of body-hardening power to create a decoy or illusion during battle. The user can make an armored version of a body part appear separately from where the real attack is coming from, tricking the opponent into blocking or dodging the wrong spot. This makes it very hard for enemies to predict real attacks, since what they see isn't always what's actually happening. It works best against fighters who rely on instinct or observation, since it directly deceives their senses. Overall, Colors Trap turns misdirection into a powerful weapon, hitting opponents when they least expect it.

Because weather affects a wide area, this style is especially useful for controlling the battlefield rather than fighting one-on-one. Overall, Art of Weather turns the natural forces around the fighter into deadly, unpredictable weapons.

cardPool.title: Honestly Impact

Because it's delivered with complete sincerity and no hesitation, the attack often catches opponents off guard despite being simple and direct. This technique works best as a finishing blow, meant to end a fight in one clean, honest hit. Overall, Honestly Impact turns pure emotion and conviction into overwhelming physical force.

cardPool.title: Life Return

It can also be used defensively, like slowing the heart rate or controlling blood flow to survive serious injuries. Because it works from the inside out, this technique doesn't rely on external tools or weapons, just complete mastery over one's own body. Overall, Life Return turns total self-control into a powerful and versatile fighting advantage.

Overall, Galaxy Impact turns raw physical force into something on a cosmic scale, hitting with truly massive power.

cardPool.title: Martial Artist
cardPool.value: Martial Artist is a straightforward fighting style based purely on physical combat skills like punching, kicking, and grappling, without weapons or special powers. It relies on years of disciplined training to build strength, speed, and precise technique. Fighters using this style often adapt classic martial arts moves, mixing them with their own personal flair or specialty. Because it depends only on the body, this style rewards raw skill, experience, and physical conditioning above all else. Overall, Martial Artist represents fighting in its purest form, where skill and hard work matter more than any special trick or tool.

The style also uses the spear defensively, blocking and parrying attacks while keeping control of the surrounding space. Overall, Spear Fighter turns distance and precision into a powerful advantage, dominating fights before they even get close.

Overall, Cyborg turns the human body into a customizable weapon, merging flesh and machine into a powerful fighting force.

cardPool.title: Swordsman
cardPool.value: Swordsman is a fighting style centered entirely on mastery of the blade, using precise cuts, thrusts, and parries to overwhelm opponents. Skilled users train for years to perfect their form, balance, and timing, turning sword strikes into fast, fluid motions. Some fighters use a single sword, while others wield two or even three at once for added speed and unpredictability. Technique often focus on cutting through defenses cleanly, aiming to end fights with a single decisive slash. Overall, Swordsman turns bladework into an art form, where precision and discipline make the sword deadlier than brute strength alone.

Built around long-range marksmanship, trick ammunition, psychological warfare, and the uncanny ability to make an impossible shot when everything is on the line. A practitioner of this style wins through wit and will, not brute force.

cardPool.title: Bofu: Blade of the void
cardPool.value: The sword of the first 20 kings, The Void Sword is not a fixed weapon but the final shape a far older one takes. Its wielder carries a jagged polearm as a matter of course, but when a fight demands a true answer, the shaft collapses and reforms into a black-edged blade  identical in silhouette to the world's finest Supreme Grade swords, yet born from something no forge ever touched. Drawing it fully requires no swing and no target: every living thing in sight, root to canopy, greys and dies in the space it takes to clear the sheath. What follows depends entirely on what the moment calls for  a single judging thrust, a storm of homing embers, a spinning double edge that turns aside lightning and steel alike, or, when nothing else will do, the sword's true and final form, which ends things outright.

cardPool.value: The sword of the first 20 kings, The only one in the collection named for a smith rather than a god or a concept, and the only one with a reputation that runs against its owner as much as its target. Blades from that name were said to be made by a man whose hatred went into the steel, and to be unwilling to return to the sheath without having cut something first. It is a superb sword. It is also patient, and it keeps a tally.

cardPool.title: Tohu: Sword of Chaos

Where its twin removes what exists, this one refuses to let anything settle into a fixed shape, including its own edge. No two cuts from it arrive the same way, which makes it very difficult to read and only slightly less difficult to aim.

cardPool.title: Oni
cardPool.value: Oni are a rare and powerful bloodline formed when humans mix with the blood of Ancient Giants, giving them a mix of human and demonic traits. They're marked by curved horns on their heads, towering height, and bodies built for brutal combat. Their strength, endurance, and durability go far beyond normal humans, letting them shrug off hits that would kill anyone else. Onis tend to have fierce, domineering personalities, often looking down on regular humans and craving conquest or absolute power. Because true-blooded Onis are so rare, most people only know them through legend, fear, or the handful of terrifying warlords who prove the myth is real.

cardPool.title: Crew Captain
cardPool.value: You start with a flag you designed yourself and a ship carrying people who chose to follow you rather than someone safer. The crew may number three or thirty, but every one of them is your responsibility, their meals, their wages, their wounds, and whatever grave the sea eventually digs for them. You give the orders, which means you also take the blame, and the moment your judgment stops being worth trusting is the moment the ship stops being yours. Somewhere ahead there's a dream big enough that you asked other people to bleed for it, and you'd better be certain it's worth what you're spending.

cardPool.title: Home Island
cardPool.value: You start where you were born, in a town that knows your name, your parents, and every stupid thing you did at twelve. Life here runs on tides and harvests and the same faces at the same tables, and nothing has ever seriously threatened that until recently. Everything you know about the wider world came secondhand from sailors passing through, half of it exaggerated and the rest of it worse than they let on. Whether you leave by choice or because something arrives and takes the choice away from you, this island is the thing you'll measure every other place against.

cardPool.title: Lost Sailor
cardPool.value: You start separated from the ship you belonged to, put ashore or washed off a deck in weather that took the decision out of everyone's hands. Your crew is somewhere out there believing you're dead, or believing you deserted, or not thinking about it at all. You know your knots, your stars, and your way around a hull, but none of that tells you which direction they sailed or whether they'd take you back. Until you find them or find something better, you're a sailor with no ship, which in most ports is another word for a beggar.

You're an outsider in a place that has clear opinions about outsiders, and every question you ask reveals a little more about how little you belong. The only way out is through, learn the rules fast, or become somebody's problem to solve.

cardPool.title: Shipwrecked

You have whatever washed up beside you and whatever this place is willing to give, and no way off it until a ship comes or you make a reason for one to. Somewhere inland there's smoke rising, and it belongs to villagers, bandits, or something with more teeth than either.

You're alive, unrecorded, and hunted by men who have never once had to explain themselves to anyone.

You survived because you were hidden, absent, or overlooked, and every year since has been spent carrying a name that gets people killed. Somewhere there are people who know exactly why it happened, and none of them intend to tell you.

The Government does not leave loose ends on purpose, which makes you a mistake they haven't corrected yet.

You ate something out of a chest on their ship without knowing what it was, and it took your ability to swim and gave you something stranger in exchange. Before they left, their captain gave up something of his own to pull you out of the water, and handed you a hat with instructions to give it back when you've become someone worth returning it to. You have been counting the years since, and you have stopped counting patiently.

Lying is the one thing you're genuinely gifted at, and you've used it to keep a sick girl smiling and a village entertained rather than to take anything from anyone. You are not brave. You just keep showing up anyway, which some people insist is the same thing.

cardPool.value: You start in a floating restaurant's kitchen, working under a one-legged cook who nearly starved to death beside you on a bare rock years ago. He gave you every scrap of food he had while telling you he had plenty, and by the time you understood what he'd done to survive it, you owed him something no wage could settle. You have never once thrown away food, you have never once raised a hand against a woman, and you have never stopped believing in a sea where every fish in the world swims together. You'll leave that kitchen someday to prove it exists.

cardPool.title: Neither One Nor the Other
cardPool.value: You start as something that no longer fits among the animals you were born with or the people you now resemble. A fruit changed your shape, and both sides decided you were a monster for it, and you spent a stretch of your life alone in the snow with that assessment for company. Someone eventually took you in, a liar, a fraud, and the first creature to look at you without flinching, and taught you medicine out of stolen books and stubbornness. You want to cure everything, and you're aware of how that sounds.

You rebuilt yourself out of scrap after that, literally, in places, and made a living dismantling ships rather than building them. Somewhere in you is the design for something meant to sail past the edge of everything, and you have never once looked at it sober.

That was decades ago. You've spent every year since drifting in fog with your own laughter for company, and the promise is still not kept, and you have not forgotten a single word of it.

cardPool.title: Cabin Boy on a Legend
cardPool.value: You start scrubbing decks on the most famous ship in the world, close enough to greatness to be splashed by it and small enough that nobody records your name. When this voyage ends, and it's going to end, you'll have to decide what to do with what you saw.

cardPool.title: Pre-Void Century Era
cardPool.value:
You start over a thousand years before anything you would recognize, in a world still whole. The seas are not yet divided into four Blues, the continents have not sunk, and the Red Line is landmass rather than a wall. There is no World Government, no Marines, no Holy Land, and no throne, only kingdoms rising independently with nobody above them. Winged people came down out of the sky generations ago and built cities on the ground. Nothing is forbidden, no stone is unreadable, and no name is dangerous to say aloud.

None of the modern cast exists. No Straw Hats, Emperors, Marines, Warlords, Roger, or Whitebeard; none will be born for a millennium.

Exists: full continents rather than islands, with the sea 200 meters lower; the All Blue, spoken of as one ocean holding all marine life; the winged people who colonized the Moon and founded Birka before descending to build Skypiea and Shandora; the Shandia in their prosperity; Alabasta already ancient and Dressrosa newly founded; the giants of Elbaf, keeping the Harley and its legends of the Warrior God and Ragnir the Iron Lightning; fish-men, merfolk, Minks, Lunarians, Buccaneers, and Sea Kings; Zunesha, already walking; the Devil Fruits, including the Sun God's; and the memory of the First World, where harnessed flame became an endless power source that bred greed and slavery, until the slaves prayed, the Sun God came, and the enraged God of the Earth joined the Serpent of Infernal Flames to drown the world in darkness.

Does not exist: the World Government, the Celestial Dragons, Mary Geoise, and the Empty Throne; the Void Century itself, with history unbroken; the Poneglyphs, uncarved, with no true history to hide; the Alliance of Twenty and its war; the four Blues, the Grand Line, and the Red Line as a dividing wall; bounties, Warlords, Emperors, and the pirate era; Impel Down, Enies Lobby, Marineford, and the auction houses; any law against speaking history; Laugh Tale and the One Piece.

cardPool.title: Void Century Era
cardPool.value:
You start inside the century that will be deleted. The Great Kingdom stands, so advanced that the greatest scientist of the future will reverse-engineer its scraps and still consider himself far beneath it. Twenty kingdoms exist alongside it as sovereign neighbors, each with its own monarch, and their alliance has not been made. There is no World Government, no Marines, no Celestial Dragons, no empty throne with anything behind it, only a ruler with ambitions and nineteen others who have agreed to nothing. The sea is still low, the continents are above water, and the histories are complete.

None of the modern cast exists. No Roger, no Whitebeard, no Straw Hats, no Marines.

Who exists: Joy Boy, the first pirate, who leads the war against the alliance; Nerona Imu, a monarch among the twenty, not yet Sovereign of the World; Nefertari D. Lily of Alabasta, who allies with them and later frees the Poneglyphs so the truth survives; the twenty monarchs, including the Figarland and Donquixote lines; the first Poseidon, whose pact with Joy Boy goes unfulfilled; the Kozuki stonemasons who carve the Poneglyphs; Kozuki Toki, who will leave this century; the robot Emet; Zunesha, tied to Joy Boy and soon sentenced; Davy D. Jones; and the Shandia, sworn to a duty they keep for eight hundred years.

What exists: the Ancient Weapons Pluton, Poseidon, and Uranus; the ark Noah; the Mother Flame; continents above a sea that will rise 200 meters this century; the D. clan, Lunarians, Buccaneers, giants, Minks, and fish-men, none yet hunted for it; and the world's complete written history, legal to read.

cardPool.title: The Great Pirate Era
cardPool.value: You start in the year the entire world went to sea. A man was executed in a harbor town and told the crowd, with the blades already at his throat, that everything he owned was theirs if they could find it, and the Government's execution became the loudest recruitment call in history. Every port is emptying of people with borrowed boats and hand-stitched flags, the Marines are expanding faster than they can train, and the sea has become the only place where an ordinary person can become anything at all. The dangerous ones haven't been sorted from the desperate ones yet, and you're indistinguishable from either.

cardPool.title: The Rocks Pirates Era
cardPool.value:
You start about forty years back, in the era before the King, when the most feared name on the sea belongs to a man who does not want treasure. Rocks D. Xebec has done what nobody has managed before or since: he has gathered captains who should have killed each other into a single crew, and he is not sailing to be remembered. He wants to rule the world, and he intends to take it off the World Government by force. The Government does not permit his name to be printed, so the world fears him without being told why.

The sea is smaller and crueler than it will be later. There is no Great Pirate Era, no Emperors, and no dream of a treasure at the end of everything, because nobody has reached the end yet. Pirates take islands rather than search for them. The Marines are outmatched and know it, and the strongest of them are still young enough to lose.

Who exists: Rocks D. Xebec, and under his flag the future Whitebeard, Kaido, Big Mom, Shiki the Golden Lion, Captain John, and others who will each become legends in their own right; Gol D. Roger and Silvers Rayleigh, rising and not yet crowned; Garp, Sengoku, Tsuru, and Zephyr, still climbing; Shanks and Buggy, young enough to be cabin boys; the Figarland line and the Celestial Dragons at the height of their arrogance; and Hachinosu, a lawless island that answers to no flag.

What exists: God Valley, an island still on the maps and about to be taken off them; the slave trade running openly under Government protection; and a Marine hierarchy that will need a hero's alliance with a pirate to survive the year.

Does not exist: the Great Pirate Era; the Four Emperors as a title; the Pirate King; Laugh Tale, reached by nobody; the Straw Hats, none of them born; any public record of Rocks, God Valley, or what happened there.

cardPool.title: The New Generation Era
cardPool.value:
You start after the old giants have begun to fall. The war that broke the world's balance is behind you, the strongest man alive is dead, and the throne he left has been taken by someone who was a rookie a few years ago. Two Emperors have been beaten in their own territory by crews nobody took seriously, the Warlord system has been abolished outright, and the Marines have lost the deterrent they spent decades building. The powers that held the sea steady for forty years are gone, retired, or busy fighting each other, and the space they left is being filled by whoever gets there first.

The sea has never been more open or more dangerous. Bounties are climbing faster than the Marines can print posters, alliances form and collapse within a season, and a name can go from unknown to Emperor-level inside a single conflict. Kingdoms are changing hands. Old crews are splintering as their captains age out or die. Everything is in motion at once.

Who exists: the Emperors of the new order, risen out of the last generation's survivors; Luffy, Law, Kid, and the rest of the rookies who crossed over together and came out the other side as powers; a Marine command rebuilding under new leadership and hunting harder to prove it still matters; the Revolutionary Army, no longer whispering, moving in the open; Blackbeard, expanding into every vacuum he can find; and Vegapunk's science, spreading faster than the Government can contain.

What exists: crews that were nobodies a year ago holding territory that belonged to legends; a Marine hierarchy stretched thin across too many fronts; Poneglyph rubbings changing hands as the race to the last island becomes a real contest.

Does not exist: the Warlord system; the old balance of power; safety anywhere; and any guarantee that whoever is on top this month will be there next.

cardPool.title: The Current Era
cardPool.value:
You start with the world already broken open. A dead scientist's broadcast told every island the truth the Government spent eight centuries burying; the sea levels are climbing; a kingdom was erased off the map in an afternoon by something nobody was supposed to know existed. The Warlord system is gone, the Emperors are no longer fighting each other so much as being circled, and the Holy Knights have been let off their leash for the first time in living memory.

The center of it is the land of the giants. The strongest warrior culture in the world, neutral through every previous war, has been invaded and is fighting back, and the King of the World came down in person rather than send anyone. That has never happened. A conflict that started as an invasion has become a war against the throne itself, and everyone still alive on that island is now a witness the Government cannot afford.

Who exists: Imu, no longer hidden, present and personally in the field; the Five Elders and the Holy Knights, moving openly; the giants of Elbaf, their elders, and the Harley that records three worlds; the Straw Hats, now Emperor-level and standing where the fight is; Shanks and his crew, active again; Blackbeard, expanding into every vacuum; Buggy's outfit; a Marine command stretched across too many fronts; and the Revolutionary Army in open war.

What exists: the true history, spoken aloud in ports that were never meant to hear it; the Ancient Weapons in play; Road Poneglyphs being gathered as the race narrows; the Mother Flame; and old powers choosing sides for the first time in eight hundred years.

Does not exist: the Government's monopoly on the truth; neutrality; anywhere far enough from the center to sit this out; and any version of the world that survives the next stretch unchanged.

Whatever comes after this will not be a change of who rules. It will be the end of the question.

cardPool.title: Random Start
cardPool.value: You start with nothing decided. This is a random start, which means your origin, your circumstances, and the situation you open in will all be chosen at random rather than by you it could be anything the world is capable of producing, common or strange, quiet or already on fire. You might wake in a village, a cargo hold, a wreck, a cell, a palace, a crew's bunk, or somewhere with no name at all, and you will learn which the same way everyone learns anything on these seas: by living the next few minutes of it. What you know is that there is water in every direction, a ship close enough to reach, and something about to happen that you did not plan for. Whatever you turn out to be, the sea will decide how much of it matters.

cardPool.title: 50 Beli Bounty
cardPool.value: You got a bounty of 50 Beli. This is not a bounty so much as a rounding error that happened to have a face attached. The clerk who processed it did not eat lunch while filling it out because the paperwork did not last long enough to finish a sandwich. Fifty Beli will not buy passage between islands, But somebody, somewhere, still put your name on paper and sent it out into the world. The Marines do not track people they have genuinely forgotten. Fifty Beli says they noticed, decided you were harmless, and filed you away, which means the only opinion standing between you and a bigger number is one they have already proven willing to change.

cardPool.title: 100 Beli Bounty
cardPool.value: You got a bounty of 100 Beli. Double what the truly forgettable get, which is technically a promotion and technically still nothing. It buys a bowl of soup, maybe two if the cook likes you. The Marine who filed it did not consider you dangerous, he considered you inconvenient, and there is a meaningful difference that the paperwork does not bother to record.  And yet the poster exists. Your face is in circulation, in files, in the stacks that Marine offices keep and never throw away. The Government does not delete names, it only revises the numbers beside them. A hundred Beli is what the world thinks you are worth right now, today, before you have given them a reason to think otherwise. Hold onto it. Every terrifying number in history had a small one printed before it.

cardPool.title: 500 Beli Bounty
cardPool.value: You got a bounty of 500 Beli. Five times what a nobody is worth, which means someone in a Marine office stopped, thought about it for a second, and then wrote down a number they were mildly confident about. That is more consideration than most people ever receive. Five hundred Beli buys a real meal, a cheap knife, or roughly one night in a bad inn. Bounty hunters still will not chase you, but they might remember the face if they see it twice, and that is a different kind of problem than being ignored. The number is small enough to laugh at and large enough to mean something changed. Somebody reported you. Somebody investigated. Somebody signed off. The Government has now spent more effort on you than the reward is worth, which tells you the reward was never really the point, the file was.

cardPool.title: 1k - 10k Beli Bounty
cardPool.value: You got a bounty somewhere between 1,000 and 10,000 Beli. This is the first number that stops being a punchline and starts being a fact. It will not make you famous, but it will make you findable. Down at the low end you are a nuisance somebody finally documented. Up near ten thousand you are a genuine local problem, the kind of name a village constable mentions with a sigh and a town drunk mentions with a grin. The reward buys a decent weapon, a week of rooms, or passage off the island if you do not mind sleeping in the hold. The difference from the coin-toss bounties is that people will now actually come. Not real hunters, not yet, but the desperate ones, the ones with nothing better lined up and a debt due Friday. They are not good and they are not careful and they will absolutely try. Somewhere a Marine has stopped filing your name under nuisance and started filing it under active, and files that move once tend to keep moving.

cardPool.title: 100k - 1 million Beli Bounty
cardPool.value: You got a bounty somewhere between 100,000 and 1,000,000 Beli. Nobody laughs at this poster. This is the range where the number stops describing what you have done and starts describing what people are afraid you will do next. At the low end you are a rookie worth watching, the kind of name that gets read aloud in a Marine briefing room without anyone reaching for coffee. At the high end you are a problem with a face, and somewhere a Captain has your poster pinned to his wall on purpose. And the Government has stopped tracking you and started planning around you. A million Beli is the threshold where they assign someone specifically. Not a patrol, a person. The number is finally big enough to be dangerous, which means so are you, which means the next thing that comes over the horizon will be something they chose deliberately to handle you.
